assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general, practical way to make aryl amines. It changed retrosynthetic planning and is used daily in pharmaceutical discovery and process chemistry. The discovery is clear and original, and its impact on synthesis is very large and lasting. Ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and related ligands) is what made it broad.
assessment.attribution: Kosugi and Migita reported early tin-amide couplings. Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic amine couplings and the ligand and mechanism work that made them general. A two-person prize on Buchwald and Hartwig is the fairest configuration, with Kosugi's precedent acknowledged but not the decisive step. I rely on my own memory of the history and have not verified the details.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of independent confirmation and industrial use. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue, though the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members cautious about a second Pd prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Nobel Prize for Pd cross-coupling may weigh against it.
Whether Kosugi/Migita precedent should share credit is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues is a new therapeutic modality built on chemistry. It turns a small molecule into a heterobifunctional tool that recruits E3 ligases and removes proteins, including targets that are hard to drug. The concept is original and the mechanism is increasingly understood, and the clinical pipeline is large.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated the first PROTAC concept. Crews developed the small-molecule PROTACs, and Ciulli's work on VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure made the approach rational. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue story (Handa, Ito, others) is a separate line and is hard to fit into three names, so the prize configuration is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials, but no PROTAC drug is approved yet. Recognition may be somewhat early, and the glue and PROTAC histories may need to be combined.
uncertainties: Several deserving contributors to the glue branch are left out of any three-person split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites as solar absorbers led to a very rapid rise in efficiency and opened a new materials class with a large worldwide research effort. The impact is considerable, although the work is more materials and device physics than molecular synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells in 2009. Park and Snaith made the solid-state devices that raised efficiency in 2012, and Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok also have strong claims, so the three-name limit forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are confirmed independently in many labs. Long-term stability and lead toxicity remain open, so commercial maturity is not yet established.
uncertainties: Stability and commercialization are not settled.
Credit is spread across many strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand cleavage, using engineered deaminase and Cas fusions. The idea is original, the chemistry of the nucleobase conversion is clear, and the impact on biology and therapy is large. It is an inventive piece of chemical protein engineering.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work and Komor and Gaudelli made the cytosine and adenine editors. Nishida and Kondo reported an independent early deaminase-Cas fusion, which complicates attribution. A Liu-led prize needs care since it is also tied to CRISPR (2020 prize).
assessment.maturity: Clinical use is starting (first base-edited patients). Recognition looks slightly early, and the 2020 CRISPR prize makes a follow-up more delicate.
uncertainties: Nishida/Kondo priority for the early fusion is not resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization addresses the central aim of efficient synthesis: using C-H bonds as functional handles and shortening routes to complex molecules. Ligand-controlled directing and template strategies gave site selectivity, and the field is a major advance in methodology.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand acceleration and distal C-H activation), Sanford (Pd(II/IV) catalysis) and Hartwig (borylation) each have decisive contributions, but the field is diffuse and Daugulis, Smith and others are also important. The set of laureates is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and increasingly used in late-stage functionalization and total synthesis, but practical generality is still limited. A well-defined discovery may be hard to isolate.
uncertainties: The discovery is a family of methods rather than a single invention.
Overlap with B043 (Hartwig) and with B001 (Bergman's earlier work).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides and thereby total chemical synthesis of proteins. It is a classic enabling idea with clear mechanism and lasting use, and it also led to expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis.
assessment.attribution: Kent, Dawson, Muir and Danishefsky made key contributions. Kent and Dawson, with Muir's expressed protein ligation, form a reasonable core, though Danishefsky's role is a debated point.
assessment.maturity: Well established for about thirty years, with many synthetic proteins made. Recognition would be timely, though impact is somewhat less universal than for cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Danishefsky's role and Brik/Liu's later extensions are not resolved.
Impact is smaller than the broadest synthetic methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions. It is now widely used in synthesis and particularly in medicinal chemistry, and it also combined with nickel and other catalysis. The impact is strong and increasing.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson reported the three early 2008-2011 breakthroughs, and Nicewicz, Fukuzumi, König and Melchiorre made important contributions. MacMillan already won in 2021 for organocatalysis, which will affect committee thinking.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted but the field is still moving, so recognition may be early, and the MacMillan prize two cycles ago weighs against it.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among many early contributors are contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (N-heterocyclic and phosphino-carbenes) showed that these species can be bottled and turned them into ligands and organocatalysts. This had a large effect on olefin metathesis catalysts, cross-coupling and main-group chemistry, and the finding is clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand isolated the first stable carbene (phosphinocarbene, 1988) and Arduengo the first crystalline NHC (1991). Nolan, Rovis and Bode are important for applications but arguably not the decisive discoverers. A two-person prize is the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent use. Timely, though the NHC impact is partly through the 2005 and 2010 prized catalyst classes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 metathesis prize in impact.
I recall the dates from memory and have not verified them.
